title: Urgent: Scaling telemetry gaps, emergency rollback protocol, and post-incident action items for dedicated pools
creator: Ravi Singh
description: Summary: A production incident on 2026-02-26 exposed a coupled set of failures in dedicated pool autoscaling and our telemetry surface. Symptoms included sustained queue growth, increasing 95th/99th latency for reserved customers, and downstream throttling that persisted for ~42 minutes before automated mitigation triggered. Impact: several Dedicated customers saw degraded throughput and intermittent 429/503 on high-throughput routes. This ticket captures the emergency response steps taken, short-term mitigations, and a concrete list of postmortem action items with owners and target dates to harden our autoscale, rollback, and telemetry behavior.
incident_timeline: 2026-02-26T03:15Z - Paging started. Primary on-call (Ava) acknowledged. Initial hypothesis: sudden traffic spike from customer A.

2026-02-26T03:20Z - Observed autoscaler did not increase desired instances for 6 minutes despite sustained queue growth; scalingEvaluator logs show repeated schedule rejection due to 'scale-cooldown' check.
2026-02-26T03:28Z - Emergency manual override issued: reserve +2 nodes to affected pool via fleet-control UI. Immediate drop in queue depth and latency begins.

2026-02-26T03:54Z - Automated mitigation policies (fallback to compatible model variant + traffic shedding) executed to protect SLA; incident declared resolved at 03:58Z after staggered recovery and verification.
root_cause_summary: Three orthogonal issues combined: (1) An unsafe cooldown policy introduced in runtime-1.18 caused scale decisions to be skipped for requests that matched a new 'burst-affinity' label; (2) Telemetry gaps in the autoscaler metrics pipeline meant we could not see instance step failures from the scheduler for ~8 minutes, delaying human diagnosis; (3) A recent release changed the backoff window semantics in the fleet-control API, which prevented manual rapid scale-up through the console unless 'override' flag was used (not exposed in the default incident runbook).
mitigations_taken: Immediate: Manual reserve of +2 nodes to affected dedicated pools via fleet-control (Ava).
Immediate: Emergency traffic policy applied to fallback customers to compatible model variant with lower memory footprint (SRE).
Short-term: Reverted the cooldown policy change in runtime-1.18 on a canary subset to verify behavior (PR: github.com/redwood/repo/pull/3284).
Short-term: Enabled lower-latency telemetry path for autoscaler (temporary toggle) to surface instance lifecycle events to PagerDuty dashboards.
postmortem_action_items: AUT-01: Rework cooldown policy logic so that burst-affinity labels do NOT opt-out of scaling decisions; owner: Priya Patel; due: 2026-03-12.

OBS-02: Add persistent instance lifecycle and scheduler failure events to the autoscaler metrics stream (high-cardinality tag set) and create a dedicated 1min dashboard; owner: Mateo Alvarez; due: 2026-03-10.
UI-03: Expose an emergency override button in fleet-control that bypasses backoff windows for on-call with MFA justification; owner: Lin Chen; due: 2026-03-18.

RB-04: Update on-call runbook for dedicated incidents to include (a) checking autoscaler 'decision_counters' (b) toggling telemetry path (c) steps to perform manual reserve; owner: SRE team; due: 2026-03-05.
TEST-05: Add end-to-end chaos tests that simulate stalled scale decisions and assert no customer-visible SLA degradation for 15min using canary traffic; owner: QA Automation; due: 2026-03-25.
METRICS-06: Implement an alert for mismatch between queue growth rate and observed scaling events (signal: queue_rate >> scale_rate for >120s); owner: Observability; due: 2026-03-09.
KB-07: Publish a post-incident walkthrough and timeline in Confluence including runbook changes and operator notes; owner: Ravi Singh; due: 2026-03-07.
risk_and_tradeoffs: Immediate rollbacks and toggles reduce blast radius quickly but can mask underlying automations—we accept short-term manual overrides with improved post-incident controls. Exposing an emergency override in the UI increases operator power; to mitigate, we add MFA and justification logging and require SRE approval for permanent use. Increasing telemetry cardinality increases ingest cost; we'll make a targeted pipeline for dedicated pools only.
acceptance_criteria: Cooldown policy change reverted and unit/integration tests covering burst-affinity behavior merged to main.
New autoscaler dashboard created and a matching alert firing during a synthetic test run.
Emergency override path implemented in fleet-control UI with MFA and audit logs; deployed to prod and verified by on-call.
Runbook updated and validated in tabletop exercise with on-call rotation.
updates: 2026-02-26 04:10 UTC - Ava: Manual reserve succeeded and latency began trending down; starting controlled revert of cooldown change on canary. Monitoring for regression.
2026-02-26 07:22 UTC - Priya: Revert PR created and started QA smoke; discovered unit test gap for burst-affinity label; added test coverage.
2026-03-01 14:45 UTC - Mateo: New metric pipeline change merged to staging; synthetic test shows lifecycle events delivered within 30s.
2026-03-03 09:12 UTC - Lin: Fleet-control emergency override UI prototype ready; design review scheduled 2026-03-04.
2026-03-05 16:00 UTC - Ravi: Draft postmortem published. Owners assigned for action items; next steps: tabletop exercise on 2026-03-10.
notes_for_reviewers: Please review the cooldown policy unit tests and the proposed alert thresholds for queue/scale mismatch. Security: the override UI will require an audit trail; reach out to Security if there are concerns about escalation policies. Suggest blocking the runtime-1.18 release until AUT-01 is resolved.
